reasons: target_missing: a play names a card whose printed effects aim at ONE enemy and carries no target, so the line cannot be replayed at all

answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I played Jumpy Dumpty first, then Kaboom! at Nibbit, spending all 3 energy. Fwoosh! was not played because it was blocked by card logic and the Spark bank was empty.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: I seriously considered Jumpy Dumpty plus Duck and Cover. That line would have gained 5 Block and reduced the telegraphed 12 damage to 7, but it would have sacrificed the 7 damage from Kaboom! for Block I did not need against a 12-damage attack.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: The chosen line gave up 5 Block from Duck and Cover. It prioritized immediate damage and leaving Nibbit at lower HP over reducing this turn's incoming damage, which is a tradeoff if a later turn or a larger attack made that Block valuable.
answers.q4_different_intent: Yes. If Nibbit's intent had been a much larger attack, especially one that could kill me or deal much more damage, I would have prioritized Duck and Cover, likely with Jumpy Dumpty, to gain 5 Block. A small attack or non-attack intent would not have changed the line.

survives_means: not yet falsified -- this funnel refuses turns and never rates them

findings.why: play 1 names 'Jumpy Dumpty', whose printed effects aim at ONE enemy, and carries no target. The bridge has nothing to aim at, so this line cannot be replayed -- it is sealed and UNTESTED, which is the state KLEESPARK-R1 ended two of its eight lines in

targets.rule: a play that names a card whose effects aim at ONE enemy must carry that enemy's printed name in `target`; a card that aims at nobody must carry `target: null`
targets.derived_from: the card sheets (understudy/resource_order.SHEETS: the three character sheets, the three companion sheets and docs/prototype-surface.yaml), read through each effect's own `target:` key. The blind packet carries NO targeting field -- the wire's hand entry has none -- so the sheet is the derivation and this is the record of it
targets.repair: out of scope by M63: this refuses a form and never repairs one

closeness_quotability: the decision-closeness gap is a falsifier reading of the TURN and is quotable under R215 B's exception; it is never evidence that a decision is fun
guardrail: staged board: this hand and this board were set by hand through a dev door, so nothing measured here is comparable to any run, and nothing here is a claim about whether the turn is fun
